title: Senior asks: delete() calls findFileActions() only to check the extension. Why?
options: So only supported files (csv, json) can be deleted, not .htaccess or other files
To choose how to delete a csv or json file
To check the file exists
To make delete faster
explain: The project only manages csv and json files. The extension check blocks delete for any other file in storage/ (for example a .gitkeep or a file you did not upload). The existence check is a different step. It is a small allow-list.

title: Senior asks: upload() first reads the temp file to validate it, then reserves a free name, then moves the file. What goes wrong if you reserve the name first?
options: A bad file leaves an empty reserved file in storage/
The name is not unique anymore
The upload gets slower
Nothing, the order does not matter
explain: reserveFreeName() creates an empty file with fopen('x'). If validation fails after that, the empty file stays in storage/. Validate first, so only valid uploads create a file.

title: Senior asks: the controller uses basename() and FileService::getPath() uses basename() again. Is the second call useless?
options: No: the service may be called from other code, so it protects itself
Yes, remove it to be DRY
No: basename is needed to add the folder
Yes: basename is slow
explain: FileService must not trust its callers. If a new controller or a CLI command forgets basename(), '../' in the name would leave storage/. Checks at every boundary are cheap defence in depth.

title: CsvFileActions::read() checks the column count before array_combine(). What does PHP 8 do if you skip the check and a row is short?
options: It throws a ValueError
It returns false
It fills the missing value with null
It returns a shorter array
explain: Since PHP 8, array_combine() throws ValueError when the counts differ. Before PHP 8 it returned false with a warning. The own check gives a clear message to the user (a 422) and not a 500.

title: array_filter keeps the keys. What does this print?
explain: array_filter() keeps the original keys. The keys are now 0, 2, 4, so the array has gaps and json_encode makes an object. Use array_values() to get a list again.

title: A static property belongs to the class, not to the object. What does this print?
code:
<?php
class Counter {
    public static int $count = 0;
    public function __construct() { self::$count++; }
}
$a = new Counter();
$b = new Counter();
echo $a::$count, ' ', $b::$count;
explain: static $count is one variable for the whole class. Both objects change the same value, so after two objects both reads give 2. Use a normal property for data of one object.

title: Promise callbacks run before setTimeout callbacks. What does Node print?
explain: Sync code first: 1 and 4. Then the promise microtask: 3. Then the timer, even with 0 ms: 2. Microtasks always run before the next timer.

title: A bad commit is already pushed to the shared main branch. What is the safest way to undo it?
options: git revert <commit> and push the new commit
git reset --hard HEAD~1 and git push --force
git commit --amend and git push --force
Delete the branch and make it again
explain: git revert adds a new commit that undoes the change. The history stays the same, so nobody has to fix their copy. reset or amend with force-push rewrites shared history and breaks the work of your team.
